scenes.narration: Think about your phone contacts. You don't memorize every phone number. You save them under names like Mom or Pizza. In Java, we do the exact same thing using variables.
A variable is like a storage box. The label on the box is the variable name. The item inside the box is the data. This label helps us find our data later.
Computers store data in memory locations with very long numbers. Instead of memorizing these numbers, we give them friendly names. This makes our code readable and much easier to manage.
To create a variable, we need three things. The data type defines what kind of data fits. The name is our unique label. Finally, the value is the actual information we store.
Look at this line of code. We start with int, which means a whole number. Then we name it score and give it the value of fifty. This creates our first variable.
The equals sign here is called the assignment operator. It does not mean both sides are equal. It means take the value on the right and put it into the box on the left.
Now we print the variable. We don't put quotes around score. If we used quotes, Java would print the word score. Without quotes, it prints the value fifty inside the box.
Let's run the program. The terminal shows fifty. Java looked for the box named score, opened it, and found the value we stored earlier. It works exactly like a contact list.
We can also change the value later. We write score equals seventy. Now, Java throws away the old value fifty and replaces it with seventy. One box can only hold one value.
Naming rules are very important. You can use letters and numbers, but you cannot start with a number. Also, you cannot use spaces or special Java keywords like class or public.
Watch what happens if we break the rules. I named this variable two-times. Because it starts with a number, Java will get confused and stop the program before it even runs.
The compiler gives us an error. It says it expected an identifier. This is a fancy way of saying your variable name is invalid. Always start your names with a letter.
To recap, variables are labeled containers. Use descriptive names and follow the starting letter rule. Your code will be much cleaner and easier for other people to understand.
